newsitem.title: CHINA: China drafts rules on public housing funds.
newsitem.headline: China drafts rules on public housing funds.

text.p: China is drafting detailed rules on the management of public housing funds, which hit 39.3 billion yuan ($4.73 billion) at the end of 1996, officials and state media said on Monday.
China's public housing funds, into which most employers and employees each pay five percent of an employee's monthly salary, were formally set up in 1994 to help workers to buy their homes.
"The drafting work has already started," an official of the Ministry of Construction said.
China had previously issued a set of brief regulations on housing funds but detailed rules were still needed, the official said. He declined to say when the new rules would be issued.
"The most important task is to ensure the safe operation of the funds," the China Business Times said, quoting Xu Hua, an official of the State Commission for Economic Restructuring.

The public housing funds would not be included in government budgetary controls, making municipal governments responsible for overseeing the funds, he said. Banks were entrusted to carry out financial transactions.
The funds should be used for extending mortgage loans to employees to buy their homes. Additional funds would be invested in treasury bonds, he said.
The rules would also prevent municipal officials from diverting the housing funds to other purposes, he was quoted as saying.
